statements.says: Reconciliation attempts in divorce cases are mandatory and held in a closed session.
At the set date the judge hears each spouse separately, then both together.
At the spouses' request a family member may attend and take part in the attempt.
If a spouse cannot attend, the judge may set a later date or delegate another judge to hear him by judicial commission.
If a spouse, personally served, fails to attend the conciliation hearing without excuse, the judge draws up a record of it.
The judge may give the spouses a period of reflection for a new attempt and order interim measures by an order not open to appeal.
In all cases the reconciliation attempts must not exceed three months from the filing of the divorce claim.
Reconciliation is recorded in a record drawn up at once by the court clerk under the judge, signed by judge, clerk and spouses, and deposited at the registry.
The reconciliation record is an enforceable instrument.
If there is no reconciliation, or a spouse fails to attend despite the reflection period, the merits of the claim are then discussed.
If no harm is proven during the proceedings, the judge may appoint two arbitrators to try reconciliation under the Family Code.
If the arbitrators achieve reconciliation, it is recorded and approved by the judge by an order not open to appeal.
The judge may end the arbitrators' mission of his own motion if it proves difficult; the case returns to the hearing.

The specialised commercial court hears six listed matters (intellectual property, commercial companies, settlement and bankruptcy, banks with merchants, maritime/air/insurance linked to commerce, international trade).

Conciliation, requested by a party and presented to the court president, precedes registration of the claim; the president appoints a judge within five days by order on petition, to conciliate within at most three months, and the requesting party notifies the other parties of the hearing date.
The appointed judge may be helped by any suitable person; conciliation ends with a record signed by judge, parties and clerk.
If conciliation fails, the claim is filed by a statement of claim with the non-conciliation record attached, on pain of inadmissibility in form.
The CPCA territorial jurisdiction rules apply to the specialised commercial court.
Parties may settle on their own or at the judge's initiative at every stage of the proceedings.
The judge holds the conciliation attempt at the place and time he finds suitable, unless a special text says otherwise.
Conciliation is recorded in a record signed by parties, judge and clerk and deposited at the court registry.
The conciliation record is an enforceable instrument once deposited at the registry.
The judge must offer mediation to the parties in all matters, except family matters, labour cases and anything touching public order.
If the parties accept, the judge appoints a mediator.
Mediation may cover all or part of the dispute and does not remove the case from the judge.
Mediation lasts at most three months, renewable once for the same period at the mediator's request after the parties' consent.
Mediation is entrusted to a natural person or an association; an association's president designates a member.
A natural-person mediator must be of good conduct, without disqualifying conviction, qualified, neutral and independent; implementing rules are by regulation.
The mediator-appointing order must record the parties' consent, the initial period and the return date.
The judge may end mediation at any time, at request or of his own motion; the case returns to the hearing.
At the end the mediator informs the judge in writing whether agreement was reached and records any agreement; the case returns on the preset date.
The judge approves the agreement record by an order not open to appeal; it is an enforceable instrument.
The mediator keeps confidentiality towards third parties.
Divorce is proved only by a judgment after several reconciliation attempts by the judge, not exceeding three months from filing.
The judge must draw up a record of the attempts and results, signed with the clerk and the parties.
A husband who takes his wife back during the reconciliation attempt needs no new contract.
If the dispute grows and harm is not proven, two arbitrators (one from each family) must be appointed and report within two months.

priorSteps.requiredWhen: In a divorce claim before the family section the judge must hold reconciliation attempts after filing (they are mandatory and divorce is proved only after them).
Before registering a claim in a matter within the specialised commercial court, conciliation must be held on a party's request to the court president.
priorSteps.sanctionIfMissing: Inadmissibility of the claim in form if the non-conciliation record is not attached.

priorSteps.requiredWhen: The judge must offer mediation to the parties in all matters; it takes place only if the parties accept. It is not a condition for filing.

sections.matter: Divorce claims and their reconciliation attempts
The six matters listed for the specialised commercial court

territory.rule: The CPCA territorial jurisdiction rules apply to the specialised commercial court.
territory.when: Claim in a matter of the specialised commercial court

exits.when: The dispute is one of the matters of intellectual property, commercial companies, settlement and bankruptcy, banks with merchants, maritime/air/insurance linked to commerce, or international trade.

openPoints.question: Does the three-month cap on reconciliation run against the claim itself or only limit the attempts, and what follows if it is exceeded?
readings: It only bounds the attempts; no sanction is stated
The judge must move to the merits once it passes

openPoints.question: Does the mandatory reconciliation of 439 apply to every family claim or only to divorce claims?
readings: Only divorce, as placed in the divorce section
Also to other claims where the Family Code requires attempts (for example khul)

openPoints.question: Who starts the periods in 536 مكرر 4 (five days, three months)?
readings: The five days run from the request and the three months from the appointment

openPoints.question: Can the court raise on its own the inadmissibility for a missing non-conciliation record?
readings: Only a party may raise it

openPoints.question: Does the exclusion of family and labour cases from mediation in 994 also bar voluntary conciliation under 990?
readings: No, 990 allows settlement at every stage
Family conciliation is governed only by 439 and following

openPoints.question: Does the mediator's period of three months run from the appointment order or from the mediator's acceptance?
